yaml.title: fast.ai Course

markdown.markdown:
<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

These are worked notebooks from the two fast.ai courses, which are deliberately taught in opposite directions.

Part 1 is top-down. You train and deploy a working model in the first lesson, then peel back layers to find out why it worked. Part 2 inverts that: it starts from matrix multiplication and rebuilds the training framework piece by piece, until the thing you have built is capable of training a diffusion model.

That second half is the reason this repo exports a library. Each foundations notebook adds to `fastAIcourse`, so by the end the package contains a small working deep learning framework assembled in course order.

---


```sh
pip install fastAIcourse
```

The library is the accumulated output of the Part 2 notebooks: `learner`, `activations`, `init`, `sgd`, `accel`, `resnet`, `augment`, `convolutions`, `datasets`, `training`, `ddpm`, `diffusion`, and `fid`. Each module comes from the notebook of the same name.

---

## Part 1: Practical Deep Learning

Top-down. A working model first, explanations after.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Getting Started](000_Intro.ipynb) | Training the first model |
| [Deployment](010_Deployment.ipynb) | Putting it somewhere people can use it, which comes second here rather than last |
| [Neural Net Foundations](020_NeuralNet.ipynb) | Stochastic gradient descent, and why linear layers plus non-linear activations are flexible enough to fit anything |
| [How a Neural Net Really Works](021_how-does-a-neural-net-really-work.ipynb) | Fitting a function with gradient descent, worked slowly |
| [Natural Language Processing](030_NaturalLanguage.ipynb) | Text classification with pretrained language models |
| [Linear Model and Neural Net from Scratch](041_linear-model-and-neural-net-from-scratch.ipynb) | No pre-built architecture, optimizer, or data loading, to see what the framework was doing |
| [Why You Should Use a Framework](042_why-you-should-use-a-framework.ipynb) | The counterargument, immediately after |
| [How Random Forests Really Work](050_how-random-forests-really-work.ipynb) | The non-neural baseline that often wins on tabular data |
| [Kaggle Tutorial](060_Kaggle_tut.ipynb) | Competing as a way of learning |
| [Multi-Target](061_multi-target.ipynb) | Predicting several things at once |
| [Collaborative Filtering](070_collaborative-filtering-deep-dive.ipynb) | Recommendation through learned embeddings |
| [Tabular Modeling](080_tabular.ipynb) | The long one, at 288 cells |
| [A Hacker's Guide to Language Models](100_lm-hackers.ipynb) | What LLMs are and how to actually use them |

---

## Stable Diffusion, Top Down

Part 2 opens by using diffusion models before explaining them.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Overview](110_Stable_Diffusion_overview.ipynb) | What the pieces are |
| [Stable Diffusion with Diffusers](111_Stable_Diffusion.ipynb) | Driving it through Hugging Face, including attention slicing to trade speed for memory |
| [Deep Dive](112_Stable%20Diffusion%20Deep%20Dive.ipynb) | Taking the pipeline apart |

---

## Part 2: Foundations

Rebuilding the framework from the bottom. Most of these notebooks export into `fastAIcourse`.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Matrix and Tensor](120_Matrix.ipynb) | Matrix multiplication, from Python loops to broadcasting, at 234 cells |
| [Backpropagation](130_Backpropagation.ipynb) | The chain rule, written out |
| [Mini-Batch Training](140_minibatch_training.ipynb) | The training loop taking shape |
| [Hugging Face Datasets](150_datasets.ipynb) | Getting data in |
| [Foundations](160_foundations.ipynb) | Callbacks and the machinery the learner needs |
| [Convolutions](170_convolutions.ipynb) | Building the operation, not calling it |
| [Learner](190_learner.ipynb) | The central abstraction that ties the loop together |
| [Activation Stats](200_activations.ipynb) | Instrumenting a model to see what its layers are doing |
| [Initialization](210_initializing.ipynb) | Why starting weights decide whether training works at all |
| [Accelerated SGD](220_accel_sgd.ipynb) | Momentum, RMSProp, Adam |
| [ResNets](230_resnet.ipynb) | Residual connections |
| [Augmentation](240_augment.ipynb) | Getting more out of the data you have |

---

## Diffusion Models

Where Part 2 lands, once the framework exists to train them.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [DDPM with miniai](250_DDPM.ipynb) | Denoising diffusion probabilistic models, the first implementation |
| [DDPM v2](270_DDPM_v2.ipynb) | The second pass |
| [DDPM v3](290_DDPM_v3.ipynb) | The third |
| [DDIM](300_DDIM.ipynb) | Implicit models, which sample in far fewer steps |
| [Karras Pre-conditioning](330_karras.ipynb) | The reformulation that made sampling schedules tractable |
| [Cosine Schedule](320_cosine.ipynb) | Choosing how noise is added over time |
| [Noise Prediction](321_noise-pred.ipynb) | Predicting how noisy a FashionMNIST image is |
| [Diffusion U-Net](360_diffusion_unet.ipynb) | The architecture doing the denoising |
| [Attention](370_attention.ipynb) | Adding attention to it |
| [Conditioned Diffusion](380_diffusion-attn-cond.ipynb) | Guiding generation with a condition |
| [FID](280_fid.ipynb) | Scoring generated images, since you cannot eyeball a distribution |

---

## Experiments and Applications

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Style Transfer](260_StyleTransfer.ipynb) | Optimising an image against a style |
| [Neural Cellular Automata](261_NCA.ipynb) | Growing an image from local update rules |
| [CIFAR-10 with Weights and Biases](310_cifar10_and_wandb.ipynb) | Classification with experiment tracking attached |
| [Tiny ImageNet](340_imgnet_tiny.ipynb) | The baseline run |
| [Tiny ImageNet, Widish](341_imgnet_tiny-widish.ipynb) | Wider, as a comparison |
| [Tiny ImageNet, Wide](342_imgnet_tiny-wide.ipynb) | Wider again |
| [Tiny ImageNet 200](343_imgnet_tiny-200.ipynb) | The full 200-class version |
| [Super-Resolution](350_superres.ipynb) | Upscaling |

---

## Not Covered Yet

- **These are course notebooks, not a reference.** They follow the lessons, so coverage is whatever the course covered and the ordering is pedagogical rather than logical. For a reference treatment see [DL Methods](https://bthek1.github.io/DL_methods/).
- **No transformer or LLM training.** Part 2 ends at diffusion; attention appears only as a component of the U-Net.
- **Several pages have placeholder titles.** [Style Transfer](260_StyleTransfer.ipynb) and [NCA](261_NCA.ipynb) are titled "Setup" and "Setup 2" internally, and the four Tiny ImageNet notebooks share one title, which is why the sidebar reads poorly.
- **The three DDPM versions are not distinguished** by their titles, so which to read is not obvious.
- **`180_autoencoder.ipynb` sits in the repo root rather than `nbs/`**, so it is neither published nor part of the library.
- The library has no documentation of its own beyond the notebooks that built it, so the exported API is only discoverable by reading them in order.

---
